SIEVE: Preserving Cross-Image Evidence via Depth-Aware Token Compression

SIEVE is a training-free method for multi-image vision-language models that uses up to 16× fewer visual tokens. At one eighth of the tokens, it retains 93–103% of the uncompressed accuracy across four open vision-language backbones, reduces prefill compute by 6.6×, and reduces the KV cache by 6.4×. It requires no fine-tuning, labeled data, or architectural changes.

The challenge of multi-image compression

Vision-language models represent each image with hundreds of tokens, while the attention component of prefill compute scales quadratically with sequence length. A four-image question on LLaVA-OneVision contains 2,916 visual tokens before any text tokens are added. Applications such as document comparison, visual question answering over image galleries, and before-and-after inspection incur this cost on every request.

Token pruning reduces this cost, but when to prune is critical. Selection before the decoder lacks question-conditioned evidence; selection at later layers incurs the cost of processing the full sequence in earlier layers. Under a budget averaged over decoder depth, retaining all tokens through layer 2 already consumes 171% of a one-sixteenth budget. The initial layers alone therefore exceed the target.

Method overview

SIEVE combines three operations in a single forward pass with frozen model weights.

  • Spatial pooling before the decoder. Average pooling reduces each image's token grid, shortening the sequence processed by the early layers. Every patch contributes to the pooled representation.
  • Question-conditioned selection. At selected decoder depths, attention from the final prompt token ranks the remaining visual tokens. An equal quota for each image prevents a single image from consuming the entire budget and eliminating evidence from others, a failure mode of global token ranking on multi-image inputs.
  • Similarity-based merging. Each removed token is merged into its most similar retained token, preserving its contribution even when an early ranking is inaccurate.

Panel (a) above illustrates the pooling and selection stages on a real question. The number of selection stages adapts to the image count, S(N) = clip(N, 2, 4): two stages for one or two images, three for three, and four for four or more.

Interactive token visualization

Select a question to explore SIEVE across decoder depths. Each image begins with 729 visual tokens, is pooled to a 10×10 grid, and is further compressed at each merging stage. Darkened regions indicate tokens that are no longer represented separately. All examples are precomputed from saved forward passes of LLaVA-OneVision-7B at a 6.25% visual-token budget, the setting used for the paper's qualitative figures.

Quantitative results

We evaluate SIEVE on nine benchmarks across four backbones. A single configuration is used throughout, without model-specific or benchmark-specific tuning.

Accuracy retained at one eighth of the visual tokens
percentage of each backbone's uncompressed five-benchmark average

At one eighth of the tokens, SIEVE retains 93–103% of each backbone's uncompressed score. It exceeds the uncompressed model by 2.01 points on LLaVA-OneVision and 1.16 points on LLaVA-1.5, illustrating how compression can reduce distracting detail alongside computational cost. Relative to the strongest competing method, SIEVE improves accuracy on 3 of the 4 backbones evaluated in the paper by 0.76 to 9.03 points, while trailing ToDRE by 1.52 points on InternVL3.

Computational efficiency

Measurements use NLVR2 on a single NVIDIA H100 with batch size 1 and no concurrent GPU workloads.

ConfigurationFLOPs (T)KV cache (MB)Prefill (ms)NLVR2
No compression20.2282.877.789.2
SIEVE, one eighth3.0812.944.188.7
SIEVE, one sixteenth1.958.143.482.7

SIEVE reduces prefill compute by 6.6× at one eighth of the tokens and 10.4× at one sixteenth. The accompanying reduction in KV cache size supports more concurrent sessions within a fixed GPU memory budget. Peak memory usage changes only slightly because model weights dominate at this sequence length; the gains come from reduced compute and cache requirements, while the model footprint remains unchanged.

Integration and applicability

  • Training-free integration. SIEVE uses the original model weights without fine-tuning, distillation, or labeled data.
  • Single-pass inference. It requires no auxiliary model, additional encoder, or draft-and-verify procedure.
  • Backbone-agnostic configuration. The same hyperparameters apply to LLaVA-OneVision-7B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen3-VL-8B, and InternVL3-8B; decoder depth is the only backbone-specific input to the schedule.
  • User-defined token budget. A closed-form schedule satisfies the chosen retention ratio, providing explicit control over the depth-averaged token budget.
  • Single-image compatibility. With one image, the per-image quota reduces to global ranking. At one eighth of the tokens, LLaVA-OneVision achieves a mean score of 71.97 across four single-image benchmarks, compared with 80.67 without compression.
